content:
Hello everyone! I'm an algebraic combinatorist, and with the help of Aristotle, I prepared a port of the beautiful library Coq-Combi in Mathlib.

After a month of polishing, I'm in a more-or-less final state, meaning that I reviewed the global structure but not the individual proofs (with a few exceptions). My branch is here.

The plan is to split it into 23 PRs (22 for Coq-Combi, plus one, independent, for q-analogs), building on top of each other, going from basic structures to the representation theory of the symmetric group. The structure is explained in the README.md (which, of course, shouldn't be ported). Each commit corresponds to a different PR; I can also include the diffs if they are useful.

If anyone can give it a brief look and give me a green light, I'll start with creating a branch each for commits 0 and 1, review the proofs, and then make a PR. Once they are ready (or at least well underway), I'll proceed with the next ones, until the whole library is ported.

Comments and critiques welcome!

How does the material on the combinatorics of representations of the symmetric group overlap/interact with the existing material on TauCeti? In general, Aristotle should not be listed as an author. Also I would not start the module doc string with the fact from where this is ported. This can be mentioned in Implementation Details.

I'm not familiar with the material on Tau Ceti, but this is a porting of a human-written library, so in principle it should be better organized.

Should I remove Aristotle both from the authors and the Copyright line, or just the former? If the latter, should I credit it in the implementation details section too?
I applied the changes to the Shuffle.lean file, if that is good I'll apply the same changes to the rest of the repository.

Alessandro Iraci said:

Should I remove Aristotle both from the authors and the Copyright line

Yes, remove from both. Fine to mention in the implementation section.

But ... it's very hard right now to get a sense of what's going on here, and how suitable this is going to be for Mathlib.

How about a branch with "one PRs worth" of material to get off the ground?

Yeah that was the plan, I was just checking for general interest before committing to review the code in detail. I also wanted to give an idea of what the end goal is, otherwise the first PR is going to look just like a bunch of pointless lemmas.
Coq-Combi appears to be GPL-licensed, is this even allowed?

I admit that I didn't think about that at all, but it's a very fair point. I should ask permission.

I opened an issue on the Coq-Combi repo. Let's wait for an answer.

Alessandro Iraci said:

what the end goal is

Licensing issues aside, what isn't clear to me from your message so far (and not having looked at the code), is that you are planning (already have?) to make sure that this integrates well/naturally with the related code that is already in Mathlib. That is much more important than being faithful to the source material.

Yes of course I am. As I said, it took a month of polishing to reach this state: the original version was a faithful porting, then I spent time removing material that was already in Mathlib, using present declarations when possible, and in general trying to transform it into something that could be integrated in the library rather than a standalone project.

I skimmed through most of the code and it looks mostly compatible with Mathlib standards, my plan was to review it PR-by-PR after the first few ones, to better understand what to aim for before investing time on polishing.

There is very little combinatorics in Mathlib, the theory of symmetric functions stops to the definition and not even in a satisfactory way. I'd like to formalize my research when publishing, but the starting point is so far behind that it is very difficult.

My end goal is to establish a solid foundation for algebraic combinatorics in the library. I thought that porting a library that was already well-thought and structured was a relatively cheap way to achieve this goal, and definitely easier than doing everything from scratch, especially when it comes to design choices. The idea was born during ItaLean in December 2025, when Aristotle was presented; I developed it recently.

Of course I'm extremely open to discussion: I'm a (mostly) new contributor, I'm happy to adapt and open to suggestions. If you think that this is a bad idea, I'm listening.

Kim Morrison said:

How about a branch with "one PRs worth" of material to get off the ground?

#43779

Alessandro Iraci said:

I opened an issue on the Coq-Combi repo. Let's wait for an answer.

Coq-Combi#22
This PR should be closed or marked draft/WIP until the licensing issue is resolved.
To be clear, this is my personal opinion. I am not a mathlib maintainer/reviewer.
I agree, merging this PR would quite clearly constitute a GPL violation
I think the chance of Coq-combi being willing or even able to relicense is very small, and so perhaps it is wise to just close this to avoid reveiwers being "poisoned" by GPLed code? (edit: closed)
I agree that the question should be postponed until the licensing issue is resolved. I'll consider an alternative roadmap independent of Coq-Combi if needed, but of course it will take much longer.
You could make your own Coq-combi port with a GPL license, the issue arises only because you are trying to merge it with mathlib

Can I? Doesn't the GPL license prevent me from changing or adapting the content of the files? Either way, my goal was to expand the combinatorics part of Mathlib, making a personal repository is not as relevant to me.

The GPL lets you modify it and redistribute it, as long as you include the original license. The issue is that while GPL projects can use Apache-licensed code, the other direction does not work (GPL has more requirements than Apache.)
I understand, thank you! Let's wait until the developers of Coq-Combi respond.

Vlad Tsyrklevich said:

while GPL projects can use Apache-licensed code, the other direction does not work

Are you sure? (of course with a IANAL caveat) I think both licenses require keeping the license, so neither direction works if you mean keeping only a single license.
Just to clarify, this PR is independent of Coq-Combi, if anyone wants to give a look!
